title: Homeowners perils, exclusions, conditions and loss settlement
summary: Follow the Millers through one Michigan January: the HO-3's perils, what it won't pay, the 80% rule, the claim clock and three tough calls.
objectives: Tell open perils from named perils, and name the six broad perils
Spot what the HO-3 won't pay: careless freezing, vandalism when vacant, critters, flood
Work the 80% replacement cost rule with real numbers
Recall the claim deadlines, where Michigan law differs, and the fraud rule

scenes.title: The Millers' very bad Michigan January
scenes.subtitle: HO-3 perils, exclusions and how a claim gets paid (2011 ISO HO-3, HO 00 03 05 11)

beats.text: It's January in Grand Rapids. Sam and Jen Miller insure their house with the 2011 HO-3, and winter is about to test it.
beats.say: It's January in Grand Rapids. Sam and Jen Miller insure their house with the twenty eleven H O three, and winter is about to test it.

scenes.title: Open perils vs named perils
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Perils Insured Against A–B; HO 00 02 10 00, Sec. I Perils
scenes.plain: Every cause of loss is covered unless the policy excludes it.
scenes.example: The Millers' house is a party: every cause gets in unless it's on the banned list. Their couch and TV: only the 16 on the guest list.
scenes.exam: HO-3: open perils on A and B (house, other structures), named perils on C. HO-2: the same 16 named perils on A, B and C.

beats.text: The Millers' house has open perils coverage: every cause of loss is covered, unless the policy excludes it.
beats.say: The Millers' house has open perils coverage: every cause of loss is covered, unless the policy excludes it.

beats.text: Their couch and TV get only 16 named perils. Not on the list? Not covered.
beats.say: Their couch and T V get only sixteen named perils. Not on the list? Not covered.

beats.text: On the exam: house open, belongings named.
beats.say: On the exam: house open, belongings named.

scenes.title: The six broad perils: one Michigan week
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Perils B.1–16; HO 00 02 10 00; adapted from memory hook mn_prop-15

draw.text: Tue: Weight of ice, snow or sleet

beats.text: Winter in Grand Rapids? Bring it on!
beats.say: Winter in Grand Rapids? Bring it on!

beats.text: Those 16 named perils cover the Millers' stuff: 10 basic, like fire and windstorm, and 6 broad.
beats.say: Those sixteen named perils cover the Millers' stuff: ten basic, like fire and windstorm, and six broad.

beats.text: Monday, crash! An icy limb falls through the roof: falling objects. Tuesday, heavy snow caves the roof in: weight of ice, snow or sleet.
beats.say: Monday, crash! An icy limb falls through the roof: falling objects. Tuesday, heavy snow caves the roof in: weight of ice, snow or sleet.

beats.text: Wednesday, the washer hose bursts: accidental discharge or overflow of water or steam. Thursday, the water heater splits: sudden and accidental tearing apart, cracking, burning or bulging.
beats.say: Wednesday, the washer hose bursts: accidental discharge or overflow of water or steam. Thursday, the water heater splits: sudden and accidental tearing apart, cracking, burning or bulging.

beats.text: Friday, the pipes freeze: freezing. Saturday, a power surge: sudden and accidental damage from artificially generated electrical current. Some come with fine print.
beats.say: Friday, the pipes freeze: freezing. Saturday, a power surge: sudden and accidental damage from artificially generated electrical current. Some come with fine print.

scenes.title: The Millers' call: what about the pipes?
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Perils Insured Against A.2 (freezing)

beats.text: Later in January, the Millers fly to a wedding during a deep freeze. Sam wants the furnace off. What else should they do?
beats.say: Later in January, the Millers fly to a wedding during a deep freeze. Sam wants the furnace off. What else should they do?

options.label: Nothing. Freezing is a named peril!
options.fail: Freezing is covered only with reasonable care: keep the heat on, or shut off the water and drain the system.

beats.text: The pipes freeze and burst. No heat, no draining: the freezing damage isn't covered.
beats.say: The pipes freeze and burst. No heat, no draining: the freezing damage isn't covered.

draw.text: Our kitchen is a skating rink!

options.label: Shut off the water, but leave the pipes full
options.fail: With the heat off, shutting off the water isn't enough: the system must be drained too.

beats.text: Water left in the pipes freezes and bursts them. Not drained, so not covered.
beats.say: Water left in the pipes freezes and bursts them. Not drained, so not covered.

draw.text: Water shut off, pipes still full

options.label: Shut off the water and drain the pipes
options.win: With the heat off, shutting off the water and draining the system is the reasonable care the policy asks for.

beats.text: Smart. No water in the pipes, nothing to freeze. That's reasonable care.
beats.say: Smart. No water in the pipes, nothing to freeze. That's reasonable care.

draw.text: Heat off? Water off and drained

reveal.text: The rule: freezing needs reasonable care: heat on, or water shut off and drained.
reveal.say: The rule: freezing needs reasonable care: heat on, or water shut off and drained.

scenes.title: Open perils on the house, but not for these
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Perils Insured Against A.2 (and its exception for accidental discharge)

draw.text: Wear and tear, rust, settling, pollutants
Water damage from plumbing or an appliance, plus tear-out

beats.text: The HO-3 also won't pay for wear and tear, rust, settling or pollutants.
beats.say: The H O three also won't pay for wear and tear, rust, settling or pollutants.

beats.text: Or for critters: birds, rodents, insects, and animals an insured owns. The Millers' dog, Biscuit, chewed the back door? Not covered.
beats.say: Or for critters: birds, rodents, insects, and animals an insured owns. The Millers' dog, Biscuit, chewed the back door? Not covered.

beats.text: The big exception: water that accidentally escapes from plumbing or an appliance is covered, including necessary tear-out.
beats.say: The big exception: water that accidentally escapes from plumbing or an appliance is covered, including necessary tear-out.

scenes.title: Vacant: the 60-day rule
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Perils Insured Against A.2.c(4); confusion pair cp_personal-08
scenes.plain: Little or no furniture or belongings inside. The stuff is gone, not just the people.
scenes.example: The Millers' neighbors moved to Traverse City and took everything. Their old Grand Rapids house sits empty while it's for sale.
scenes.exam: No vandalism coverage on the house if it was vacant more than 60 consecutive days before the loss. Under construction isn't vacant.

draw.text: Millers away, furniture home: unoccupied, not vacant

beats.text: Next door, a word the exam loves: vacant. It means little or no furniture or belongings inside.
beats.say: Next door, a word the exam loves: vacant. It means little or no furniture or belongings inside.

beats.text: The neighbors moved to Traverse City and took everything.
beats.say: The neighbors moved to Traverse City and took everything.

beats.text: If a house was vacant more than 60 consecutive days before the loss, vandalism to the house isn't covered. A house under construction isn't vacant.
beats.say: If a house was vacant more than sixty consecutive days before the loss, vandalism to the house isn't covered. A house under construction isn't vacant.

beats.text: Watch out: the Millers at the wedding, furniture still home? That's unoccupied, not vacant.
beats.say: Watch out: the Millers at the wedding, furniture still home? That's unoccupied, not vacant.

scenes.q: The neighbors' house, insured under the 2011 HO-3, has been vacant for 70 consecutive days. Then vandals spray-paint the walls. The vandalism loss to the house is:
scenes.why: Coverages A and B exclude vandalism and malicious mischief if the dwelling was vacant more than 60 consecutive days before the loss.

beats.text: Quick check: 70 days vacant, then vandals. Covered?
beats.say: Quick check: seventy days vacant, then vandals. Covered?

reveal.text: Not covered: 70 days is more than 60 consecutive days vacant.
reveal.say: Not covered: seventy days is more than sixty consecutive days vacant.

scenes.title: The nine Section I exclusions
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Exclusions A.1–9; adapted from memory hook mn_prop-22
scenes.hook: Old Ernie's Wet Pontoon Never Went North In Grayling.
items: Ordinance or law; Earth movement (like an earthquake or sinkhole); Water
Power failure off premises; Neglect (not protecting property at and after a loss); War
Nuclear hazard; Intentional loss (an insured meant it); Governmental action (seizure, destruction)
Water: flood, surface water, sewer or drain backup, sump overflow, subsurface water

beats.text: One Michigan sentence holds all nine Section I exclusions: Old Ernie's Wet Pontoon Never Went North In Grayling.
beats.say: One Michigan sentence holds all nine Section one exclusions: Old Ernie's Wet Pontoon Never Went North In Grayling.

beats.text: Ordinance or law, earth movement like an earthquake, water. Power failure off premises, neglect, war. Nuclear hazard, intentional loss, governmental action.
beats.say: Ordinance or law, earth movement like an earthquake, water. Power failure off premises, neglect, war. Nuclear hazard, intentional loss, governmental action.

beats.text: Water includes flood, sewer or drain backup, and sump overflow.
beats.say: Water includes flood, sewer or drain backup, and sump overflow.

beats.text: And all nine apply no matter what other cause contributes.
beats.say: And all nine apply no matter what other cause contributes.

scenes.title: Which water is covered?
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Perils A.2 exception; Sec. I Exclusions A.3 Water; question prop-048

items.text: The washer hose bursts and soaks the laundry room
items.why: Accidental discharge from an appliance: the water damage is covered (not the hose itself).

items.text: The Grand River floods the basement
items.why: Flood is part of the Water exclusion.

items.text: A pipe in the wall bursts and soaks the drywall
items.why: Accidental discharge from plumbing: the water damage is covered, plus necessary tear-out.

items.text: Sewage backs up through the floor drain
items.why: Sewer or drain backup is part of the Water exclusion.

items.text: Heat on, but a frozen pipe bursts and soaks the floor
items.why: Heat was maintained, so the freezing damage is covered.

items.text: The sump overflows into the basement
items.why: Sump overflow is part of the Water exclusion.

beats.text: Your turn, a classic exam trap: covered, or excluded?
beats.say: Your turn, a classic exam trap: covered, or excluded?

reveal.text: Water damage from plumbing or an appliance is covered.
reveal.say: Water damage from plumbing or an appliance is covered.

reveal.text: Flood, drain backup and sump overflow are excluded.
reveal.say: Flood, drain backup and sump overflow are excluded.

scenes.title: The 80% rule: paying for Sam's roof
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Cond. D.2.a–b, d; memory hook mn_prop-21; ACV: confusion pair cp_personal-05

beats.text: The adjuster comes. Insure to at least 80% of replacement cost, and house losses are paid at replacement cost, no depreciation.
beats.say: The adjuster comes. Insure to at least eighty percent of replacement cost, and house losses are paid at replacement cost, no depreciation.

beats.text: Fall short, and you get the greater of two amounts. One is actual cash value, or ACV: usually new cost minus depreciation.
beats.say: Fall short, and you get the greater of two amounts. One is actual cash value, or A C V: usually new cost minus depreciation.

beats.text: The other is did over should: what you did carry, over what you should carry, times the repair cost.
beats.say: The other is did over should: what you did carry, over what you should carry, times the repair cost.

beats.text: Rebuilding costs $250,000, so Sam should carry 80% of that: $200,000. He carries $150,000.
beats.say: Rebuilding costs two hundred fifty thousand dollars, so Sam should carry eighty percent of that: two hundred thousand dollars. He carries one hundred fifty thousand dollars.

beats.text: Did over should is three quarters. The repair costs $20,000, so he gets $15,000 once it's fixed. That beats the ACV, $12,000.
beats.say: Did over should is three quarters. The repair costs twenty thousand dollars, so he gets fifteen thousand dollars once it's fixed. That beats the A C V, twelve thousand dollars.

beats.text: Ignore the deductible here. Your turn: slide to the smallest limit that pays all $20,000.
beats.say: Ignore the deductible here. Your turn: slide to the smallest limit that pays all twenty thousand dollars.

reveal.text: $200,000: exactly 80%. Meet the test, and the whole repair is paid, not 80% of it.
reveal.say: Two hundred thousand dollars: exactly eighty percent. Meet the test, and the whole repair is paid, not eighty percent of it.

scenes.title: Sam's call: take the ACV now?
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Cond. D.2.d–e

draw.text: ACV today: $12,000. The rest? Tell us within 180 days.

beats.text: ACV today: $12,000. For the rest, tell us within 180 days of the loss that you'll repair.
beats.say: A C V today: twelve thousand dollars. For the rest, tell us within one hundred eighty days of the loss that you'll repair.

beats.text: What should Sam do?
beats.say: What should Sam do?

options.label: Demand the full $15,000 before any repairs
options.fail: Until repairs are done, only ACV is paid, unless the loss is under 5% of the insurance and under $2,500. $20,000 isn't.

beats.text: The insurer says no. Before repairs, it pays only ACV.
beats.say: The insurer says no. Before repairs, it pays only A C V.

options.label: Take $12,000; next month, say he'll repair
options.win: Take the ACV now, then claim the rest: give notice within 180 days after the loss that you'll repair.

beats.text: Smart. Sam takes $12,000 now and collects the rest after repairs.
beats.say: Smart. Sam takes twelve thousand dollars now and collects the rest after repairs.

options.label: Take $12,000; bring up repairs a year later
options.fail: To claim the rest after taking ACV, Sam must give notice within 180 days after the loss.

beats.text: Too late: he missed the 180-day window.
beats.say: Too late: he missed the one hundred eighty day window.

beats.text: There was a deadline?
beats.say: There was a deadline?

reveal.text: Under the 2011 form, until repairs are done, you get only ACV, unless the loss is under 5% of the insurance and under $2,500.
reveal.say: Under the twenty eleven form, until repairs are done, you get only A C V, unless the loss is under five percent of the insurance and under two thousand five hundred dollars.

scenes.title: The claim clock, and one deductible rule
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Cond. B, C.8, H, I, J; MCL 500.2833(1)(p)–(q)

draw.text: Proof of loss: 60 days after they ask
Insurer: 30 days to choose repair or replace
Michigan: pay within 30 days of proof (form: 60)
Suit: 2 years (form). Michigan pauses it, notice to denial
Two deductibles? Only the highest applies

beats.text: Sam sends a sworn proof of loss within 60 days after the insurer asks. The insurer then has 30 days to choose to repair or replace.
beats.say: Sam sends a sworn proof of loss within sixty days after the insurer asks. The insurer then has thirty days to choose to repair or replace.

beats.text: Payment: the 2011 form says 60 days, but Michigan law says 30 days after proof of the amount of loss.
beats.say: Payment: the twenty eleven form says sixty days, but Michigan law says thirty days after proof of the amount of loss.

beats.text: Suit: 2 years under the 2011 form, longer than Michigan's 1-year minimum, so it stands. Michigan tolls, or pauses, that clock from notice of loss until formal denial.
beats.say: Suit: two years under the twenty eleven form, longer than Michigan's one-year minimum, so it stands. Michigan tolls, or pauses, that clock from notice of loss until formal denial.

beats.text: One deductible rule: if two apply to one loss, only the highest applies.
beats.say: One deductible rule: if two apply to one loss, only the highest applies.

scenes.title: Which clock?
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Cond. C.8, H, I, J; MCL 500.2833(1)(p)–(q)

items.text: Sam sends his sworn proof of loss, after they ask
items.why: Sworn proof of loss (a signed, sworn statement of the loss): within 60 days after the insurer's request.

items.text: The insurer says it will repair or replace
items.why: Our Option: written notice within 30 days after the sworn proof of loss.

items.text: Loss payment under the unendorsed 2011 form
items.why: The form: 60 days after proof of loss plus an agreement, judgment or appraisal award.

items.text: In Michigan: payment after proof of the amount of loss
items.why: Michigan law: payment within 30 days after proof of the amount of loss.

items.text: Sam sues the insurer over the claim
items.why: Suit: within 2 years after the loss under the 2011 form. Michigan tolls it from notice of loss until formal denial.

beats.text: Your turn: which clock?
beats.say: Your turn: which clock?

reveal.text: Proof of loss and the form's payment: 60 days. The insurer's notice to repair or replace, and Michigan payment: 30. Suit: 2 years.
reveal.say: Proof of loss and the form's payment: sixty days. The insurer's notice to repair or replace, and Michigan payment: thirty. Suit: two years.

scenes.title: Sam's call: the couch the snow missed
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Cond. R, Sec. II Cond. J; MCL 500.2833(2) case law (Wilson, E.D. Mich. 2019)

beats.text: Tuesday's cave-in missed the old couch. But Sam could claim the snow crushed it. What should he do?
beats.say: Tuesday's cave-in missed the old couch. But Sam could claim the snow crushed it. What should he do?

options.label: Claim it. Only Sam would be on the hook
options.fail: Concealment or Fraud: if any insured lies about or hides a material fact, no insured gets Section I coverage, honest Jen included.

beats.text: Busted. Now no insured gets Section I coverage, not even Jen.
beats.say: Busted. Now no insured gets Section one coverage, not even Jen.

draw.text: Property coverage: no insured, not Sam, not Jen

options.label: Report only what really broke
options.win: Honest claim, no trouble. One insured's fraud would have cost every insured their Section I coverage.

beats.text: Good call. The roof claim stays on track, and Jen stays covered too.
beats.say: Good call. The roof claim stays on track, and Jen stays covered too.

reveal.text: One insured's lie costs every insured their Section I property coverage. Under Section II, liability, only the insured involved loses it.
reveal.say: One insured's lie costs every insured their Section one property coverage. Under Section two, liability, only the insured involved loses it.

reveal.text: In Michigan, though, courts require coverage for an innocent co-insured's fire loss. None of the Millers' losses this January was a fire.
reveal.say: In Michigan, though, courts require coverage for an innocent co-insured's fire loss. None of the Millers' losses this January was a fire.

items: HO-3: open perils on the house, 16 named perils on belongings
Freezing: heat on, or water off and drained. Flood: excluded
Vacant over 60 days in a row: no vandalism to the house
Under 80%: greater of ACV or did over should times the loss
Fraud: Section I lost for all. Michigan: pay within 30 days of proof

beats.text: What a week! Open perils on the house, minus the exclusions. Heat on, or shut off and drain. Vacant over 60 days? No vandalism to the house.
beats.say: What a week! Open perils on the house, minus the exclusions. Heat on, or shut off and drain. Vacant over sixty days? No vandalism to the house.

beats.text: Under 80%, it's the greater of ACV or did over should.
beats.say: Under eighty percent, it's the greater of A C V or did over should.

beats.text: And Sam? No fibbing. Also, we're raising our limit.
beats.say: And Sam? No fibbing. Also, we're raising our limit.

sources: MCL 500.2833(2); Wilson v. State Farm (E.D. Mich. 2019)
